title: Choose the Quick Panel composition
question: The visual world is fixed; choose which hierarchy should become Clickity’s production layout.

options.label: Ready First
options.thesis: The current state and Start action dominate, making Clickity feel immediate every time it opens.
options.viewport: A commanding ready panel owns the top third; settings follow as broad rows with contextual coordinates.
options.risk: The main action is exceptionally clear, but the interval details become one step less visible.

options.label: Interval First
options.thesis: The four-part interval becomes Clickity’s signature control while the action remains fixed at the bottom.
options.viewport: A continuous hours-to-milliseconds strip leads, followed by three compact mode rows and a sticky action dock.
options.risk: This is fastest for precise setup, but gives runtime status less visual space than Ready First.

options.label: Balanced Split
options.thesis: Timing and behavior stay visible together, creating the clearest overview of the complete configuration.
options.viewport: A wider timing column and narrower behavior column share the window above a contextual coordinate tray and full-width action.
options.risk: It exposes the most information, but has the densest visual rhythm of the three.
